title: Square-zero extension classes are unchanged by completion off a smooth open
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $B$ be a finite-type commutative $k$-algebra, let $J\subseteq B$ be an ideal, and suppose $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is smooth over $k$ on the complement of $V(J)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $N$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Put $\widehat B=\varprojlim_nB/J^n$ and $\widehat N=\varprojlim_nN/J^nN$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Write $\operatorname{Exal}_k(B,N)$ for the isomorphism classes of exact sequences of $k$-algebras and modules $0\to N\to E\to B\to0$, where the kernel is an ideal with square zero and its induced $B$-module structure is the specified one; isomorphisms induce the identity on both $N$ and $B$. This is an abelian group under Baer sum, with its natural $k$-vector-space structure. Completing $E$ along the inverse image of $J$ induces a canonical $k$-linear isomorphism $\operatorname{Exal}_k(B,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Exal}_k(\widehat B,\widehat N)$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ4 (lemma-first-order-completion), including the Exal notation immediately preceding it and the natural additive structure there.

proof.text: Every ideal of the field $k$ is zero or $k$, so $k$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $B$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-polynomial-simplicial-resolution] to obtain a resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ with $P_n=k[x_1,\ldots,x_{r_n}]$, each $r_n$ finite. The comparison of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] identifies $L=L_{B/k}$ in $D(B)$ with the alternating differential complex with terms $B\otimes_{P_n}\Omega_{P_n/k}$ in degree $-n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension] these terms are $B^{r_n}$: apply it to $k\to k$, whose differential module is zero since a $k$-derivation vanishes on every element of $k$. Thus $L$ has a bounded-above finite-free representative and is pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 0DZ4 (lemma-first-order-completion), proof and preceding Exal notation.

proof.text: Write $T^i(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(L,M[i])$. By [lem-sfb-cotangent-ext-smooth-support], for every finite $B$-module $M$ and every $i\geq1$, $T^i(M)_{\mathfrak p}=0$ when $\mathfrak p\notin V(J)$, since those primes are smooth by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-supported-complex-ext-completion] with $A=B$, $I=J$, $K=L$ and $a=1$. In particular the coefficient map $c:T^1(N)\to T^1(\widehat N)$ is an isomorphism, and the maps $T^1(N)\to T^1(N/J^nN)$ are jointly injective.

source.place: Tag 0DZ4 (lemma-first-order-completion), proof and preceding Exal notation.

proof.text: Let $0\to N\to E\xrightarrow p B\to0$ be an extension and $H=p^{-1}(J)$. The kernel $N$ is a finitely generated ideal of $E$: lift the coefficients in an expression using its finite $B$-module generators. Since $N^2=0$, its adic completion is $E$ itself. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] to $E,N$, with quotient $B$ Noetherian, to see that $E$ is Noetherian. Regard this sequence as finite $E$-modules (the actions on $N,B$ factor through $B$). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] for $E,H$ gives $0\to\widehat N\to\widehat E\to\widehat B\to0$, since $H^nN=J^nN$ and the image of $H^n$ in $B$ is $J^n$. The kernel remains square zero: its components in $E/H^n$ are represented by elements of $N$, whose products vanish. This defines the completion map $F$ on classes. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete], $\widehat B$ is Noetherian and complete for $J\widehat B$, with $\widehat B/J^n\widehat B=B/J^n$ and $\widehat N/J^n\widehat N=N/J^nN$. The kernel $\widehat N$ is finite over $\widehat B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor]: a finite set of generators of $N$ gives generators $1\otimes n_i$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ4 (lemma-first-order-completion), proof and preceding Exal notation.

proof.text:
Use [lem-sfb-ring-square-zero-extension-classification] to identify classes with $T^1$ and to identify pushout, pullback and Baer sum. The canonical map $E\to\widehat E$, inducing $B\to\widehat B$ and $N\to\widehat N$, implies
$$\operatorname{res}(F([E]))=c([E])\quad\text{in }T^1(\widehat N).$$
Here $\operatorname{res}$ pulls an extension of $\widehat B$ back along $B\to\widehat B$. It is injective: if $0\to\widehat N\to D\xrightarrow q\widehat B\to0$ pulls back to a split extension, choose its $k$-algebra lift $\sigma:B\to D$. The kernel $\widehat N$ is a finite ideal by step 3 and is square zero, so its completion is $D$; [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] implies $D$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-square-zero-adic-thickening] to $D$, its kernel, and $H_D$, using completeness of its quotient $\widehat B$ from step 3. Thus $D$ is complete for $H_D=q^{-1}(J\widehat B)$. Since $\sigma(J)\subseteq H_D$, it induces compatible maps $B/J^n\to D/H_D^n$. Their inverse limit, followed by the inverse of $D\to\varprojlim D/H_D^n$, gives $\widehat\sigma:\widehat B\to D$. Its composite with $q$ is the identity: on each quotient by $J^n\widehat B$ it is the projection $\widehat B\to B/J^n$, and these projections are jointly injective by step 3. It is a $k$-algebra map because all the quotient maps are. Thus $D$ splits. Pullback preserves Baer sum by the classification, so trivial kernel proves injectivity of $\operatorname{res}$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ4 (lemma-first-order-completion), proof and preceding Exal notation.

proof.text: For every completed extension class $y$, step 2 supplies a unique $x$ with $c(x)=\operatorname{res}(y)$. The identity in step 4 gives $\operatorname{res}(F(x))=\operatorname{res}(y)$, hence $F(x)=y$ by injectivity of restriction. If $F(x)=0$, the same identity gives $c(x)=0$, whence $x=0$. Finally $\operatorname{res}$ and $c$ preserve addition and multiplication by every $a\in k$: addition is Baer sum, and scalar multiplication is pushout along $a:N\to N$ (or $a:\widehat N\to\widehat N$), all respected by [lem-sfb-ring-square-zero-extension-classification]. Therefore $\operatorname{res}(F(x+x'))=\operatorname{res}(F(x)+F(x'))$ and $\operatorname{res}(F(ax))=\operatorname{res}(aF(x))$; injectivity of restriction proves the two equalities before restriction. Thus the specified completion map is a canonical $k$-linear isomorphism.

The item statement is unchanged, it is a first split (no repair note), and live and side-live still have it unsplit, so nothing supersedes it. Step 1: the finite polynomial resolution plus the cotangent coherence comparison, with Ω of a polynomial ring free of rank r_n, gives a bounded-above finite-free representative of the full L, so L is pseudo-coherent. Step 2: the smooth-support node gives the localization vanishing at every prime off V(J), which is exactly the hypothesis of the new supported-complex node, so the coefficient map c is an isomorphism. Step 3: E is Noetherian by 05GH because N is a finite square-zero ideal (Stacks omitted this); exactness of completion over (E, p^{-1}J) uses H^nN = J^nN and p(H^n) = J^n, both checked. Step 4: the classification criterion gives res∘F = c. Injectivity of res: D is Noetherian by 05GH, complete by the thickening node, σ(J) ⊆ H_D, the limit map σ^ satisfies qσ^ = id by separatedness of the completed base, so D splits. Step 5: an elementary group chase gives bijectivity and k-linearity. Both new nodes are true and strictly smaller than the item. The thickening node is 0DYC with I = Q, Q^2 = 0; its proof is not elementary and no 0DYC node exists in the DAG. The supported-complex node follows from 0DYJ (finite module with support in V(I) is killed by a power of I) and from 0A6A(3), adjunction and torsion invariance under completion; its inverse-limit clause is unused by the item but true. A DAG-wide scan found no duplicate of either node; searches are recorded with all three tool kinds.
